summary: Build a website that provides access to "Clash Royale unblocked" for the user.
known_issues: Branding rename to "ClashRoyaleHub" did not update the link name/label; link still shows the old name after Version 7 launch.

existing_features.title: Do not implement, host, embed, proxy, or provide any mechanism to bypass network restrictions, paywalls, or access controls (“unblocked” gameplay) for Clash Royale; instead, present a clear message that the site only provides legal, official access options and informational content.

Build a responsive public website with a homepage that provides (a) a brief description of Clash Royale, (b) prominent buttons linking to official ways to play (e.g., official app store pages and the official Clash Royale website), and (c) a simple navigation layout (Home, Beginner Guide, Deck Tips, About).
Add static content pages/sections in English: a Beginner Guide (basic mechanics, elixir, towers, win conditions) and Deck Tips (general principles like average elixir, synergy, counters).

Create and apply a coherent, distinct visual theme (colors, typography, spacing, components) appropriate for a competitive card-battle game companion site; avoid using blue/purple as the primary palette.
Add a lightweight optional feedback form (name/email optional + message) that stores submissions in the Motoko backend for later review.

Expand the "Deck Tips" page by adding a new section that lists multiple concrete example decks (more than what exists today) as static content, with each deck including: deck name, archetype, approximate average elixir, a list of the 8 cards (as text), and short bullet points for basic gameplan and key strengths/weaknesses.

Add visible site attribution text stating: "Created by Franklin Holmes and Lincoln Wood" in a consistent, non-intrusive location on the site (e.g., within the global footer) so it appears across all pages.
Add a new user-facing chat page that introduces a free assistant named "Fred" and lets users ask questions about Clash Royale in a chat-style interface (message history + text input + send action).

Implement Fred responses locally (no network calls) using a deterministic rules/FAQ knowledge base focused on Clash Royale fundamentals, decks, and site content, with safe fallbacks for unknown questions.
Update the app’s simple page-based routing and SiteLayout navigation types to include the new Fred chat page while keeping the existing pages and admin-only navigation behavior intact.

Add an on-page disclaimer on the Fred chat page stating that Fred is an offline helper with limited knowledge, provides informational guidance only, and is not affiliated with Supercell; also reiterate that the site does not provide “unblocked” gameplay or bypass methods.
Add a simple, user-friendly welcome/intro screen to the "Ask Fred" page (FredChatPage) that clearly explains what users can ask and provides a clear call-to-action to start chatting.
Persist the Ask Fred welcome/intro screen dismissal so it does not reappear every time the user navigates away and back during typical use.

Expand Fred’s deterministic, offline Clash Royale knowledge base so he can answer substantially more questions beyond the current topics, while keeping all responses fully local (no network calls) and rules-based.

Improve Fred’s intent/keyword matching so that common variations, synonyms, and card/deck-related phrasing are more reliably routed to the best available answer, without introducing nondeterministic behavior.

Update the Ask Fred UI helper text to reflect Fred’s expanded offline topic coverage (welcome intro topic cards and the in-chat descriptive text), keeping all user-facing text in English and consistent with the existing disclaimer about being offline and not affiliated with Supercell.

Enforce basic posting permissions for discussions: allow anyone to read threads/comments, but require Internet Identity authentication to create threads or post comments/replies, with clear error messages for unauthenticated users.
Create a new frontend page for Discussions that lets users browse threads, open a thread detail view, and participate via posting new threads and threaded comments (replies).
Integrate Discussions into the existing page-based routing and navigation without breaking existing pages (Home, Beginner Guide, Deck Tips, Ask Fred, About, Admin).

Add React Query hooks/mutations for discussions to fetch thread lists, fetch a thread with comments, create a thread, create a comment, and create a reply; ensure caches invalidate appropriately after posting so new content appears after submission.

Add lightweight content safety/abuse guardrails: enforce reasonable maximum lengths for thread titles/bodies and comment bodies, and reject empty/whitespace-only submissions in both frontend validation and backend validation.
Update the website name/branding to “Clash Royale Hub” anywhere it is user-visible, including the HTML document title, so the browser tab title matches the site header branding.

Update all user-visible branding text that currently shows the site name as "Clash Royale Hub" so it displays exactly "ClashRoyaleHub" (no spaces), including the header brand label and the HTML document title.

new_feature_requests.summary: Create a site that hosts/provides access to Clash Royale in an "unblocked" manner.
Add more Deck Tips/deck examples to the site (create additional decks content).
Add site attribution/credits text stating it was created by Franklin Holmes and Lincoln Wood.
Add an in-site free AI chat assistant named "Fred" that users can ask Clash Royale questions.
Add a simple welcome screen/intro on the Fred chat page so users know they can ask Fred anything.
Expand Fred’s offline knowledge base so he can answer a lot more Clash Royale questions (broader, more detailed coverage).
Add a Reddit-style comment/discussion system so users can chat about Clash Royale on the site (threaded comments, posting, and viewing discussions).
Add backend support for a Reddit-style discussion system with (a) discussion threads and (b) threaded comments/replies, stored in the Motoko canister and accessible via Candid methods.
Rename the website to "Clash Royale Hub" (update site name/branding).
